basis: Neurodevelopmental disability and strabismus define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 22/24. Hearing impairment and endocrine findings are occasional.
Benign neoplasm located in the central nervous system; no additional organ involvement applies across the umbrella.
Immune-mediated psoriatic disease defined by inflammatory arthritis associated with cutaneous or nail psoriasis.
Inherited ventricular arrhythmia; syncope reflects impaired cardiac output rather than a separate neurologic disorder.
Focal epilepsy with impaired awareness arises from cerebral seizure activity.
Defined cortical cognitive deficits associated with parietal white matter injury.
Absent limbs define disease; oral clefts and renal agenesis each 2/3; choanal atresia 1/3, pulmonary hypoplasia reported. Ocular, adrenal and splenic defects omitted by cap.
Malignancy of precursor T lymphoblasts spanning leukemia and lymphoma; refractory status adds no organ axis.
Skeletal dysplasia with limb malformations defines the syndrome; pendular nystagmus affects ocular function in 2/2 reported patients.
Inherited macular degeneration with retinal lesions, macular atrophy and reduced visual acuity.
Inherited coagulation defect; intracranial and joint hemorrhage each annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting brain and joint injury. Epistaxis alone adds no airway axis.
Cutaneous sweat duct obstruction produces the defining vesicular or papular eruption.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and dilated cardiomyopathy define the syndrome. Minor digit and external-ear morphology do not establish functional damage.
P5CS-related metabolic disorder presenting as progressive spastic paraplegia and neuropathy. Cataracts are occasional; pes cavus accompanies neurologic dysfunction.
Chronic fungal or bacterial infection of subcutis; bone abnormalities and structural foot deformity are frequent (30-79%), supporting destructive local extension.
Benign adipose tissue tumor of the axillary soft tissue; subcutis belongs to the dermatologic axis.
Ciguatoxin poisoning is defined by gastrointestinal, neurologic and cardiovascular dysfunction; toxin exposure is not an infection.
Carcinoma originates in the epithelium of the middle ear.
Severe cerebral malformation defines disease. Scalp folds in 2/2 do not establish skin dysfunction; amyotrophy accompanies profound neurologic impairment.
Congenital loss of smell from abnormal olfactory development; smell belongs to the neurologic axis. No endocrine disease is intrinsic to this isolated condition.
Odontogenic epithelial neoplasm of the jaws, involving the tooth-forming apparatus and jaw bone.
Inherited follicular hamartomas with papules, hypotrichosis and palmoplantar pits are confined to skin and its appendages.
Pentose phosphate metabolic defect with developmental delay (5/5) and congenital heart defects (4/5); cataracts occur in 2/5 and uveitis is frequent (30-79%).
Scalp aplasia (10/11), enamel hypoplasia (9/9) and developmental disability define the syndrome; cataracts affect 5/10.
Infantile myofibroblastic tumors characteristically arise in skin, subcutis and musculoskeletal soft tissues; visceral involvement is a minority manifestation.
